s: Recovery is real; the price asks for more
Initiate with Underweight and a November 2027 price target of INR200,
implying 24.4% downside from the INR264.57 NSE reference close on 4
November. Our target is 22x FY28 EQe diluted parent EPS of INR9.07. The
business is recovering; the current valuation already anticipates a substantial
Q2 FY27 operating revenue increased 16.3% to INR2,838 crore. EBITDA
excluding other income rose to INR338 crore, or 11.9% of sales. Parent PAT
was INR169.10 crore, against INR12.98 crore a year earlier. Management's
INR2,870 crore headline revenue is total income; its INR370 crore EBITDA
We forecast FY27/FY28 operating revenue of INR11,400/12,600 crore and
operating EBITDA margins of 12.0%/13.0%. This assumes export demand
improves, domestic brands grow and Flooring earns better returns. These are
Equinox scenarios, not company guidance or consensus.
The cash recovery needs perspective. H1 operating cash flow of INR1,101
crore includes INR617 crore of working-capital inflow. Trade payables alone
contributed INR525 crore. A repeat of that release is not embedded in our
earnings thesis. Lease liabilities also remain despite the reported net-cash
The key upside risk is a stronger structural margin reset. At 25x earnings, a
bull case with 15% operating EBITDA margin supports approximately
INR305. The base case needs continued execution but produces only INR200
at 22x. Cotton, trade policy, customer concentration and Vapi restoration

Recovery has breadth, but the base is depressed
Q2 Home Textiles segment revenue was INR2,689.02 crore and Flooring revenue INR216.23 crore, before INR67.13 crore
of intersegment eliminations. Flooring segment EBITDA increased to INR23.42 crore from INR3.75 crore. This is
evidence of operating improvement, while the very low prior-year earnings base exaggerates percentage PAT growth. [S1
Brands and onshore capacity are useful options
Management reported 28.2% domestic growth, 18.3% home-textile export growth and 2.4x growth in the US pillow
business in Q2. These are management operating indicators; they do not establish group organic growth or a separately
valued brand asset. Our base case gives no incremental sum-of-parts premium. [S1 pp2-3]
The multiple must reflect manufacturing risk
A 22x forward P/E implies a 4.55% earnings yield. It allows for recovery beyond FY26 but recognises cyclical demand,
reinvestment and concentrated customers. The sensitivity spans 18-28x; none is represented as a verified trading-peer
average. Trident and Indo Count would be relevant home-textile comparators; different product mix, balance sheets and
fiscal definitions prevent a casual multiple comparison.
Reconsider the cautious rating if sustained operating EBITDA margins exceed 14%, FY28 parent EPS moves above
INR10.6 and earnings retain a 25x multiple, or the price falls enough to restore prospective returns. A lower share price
alone does not validate the earnings forecast. Watch operating revenue, EBITDA excluding other income, cash conversion
excluding working-capital release, and actual Vapi restoration.
FY27 incorporates reported H1 and INR7.16cr exceptional loss. No further insurance/tariff windfall assumed. No forward cash-flow/balance-sheet claim.

Cash conversion and the net-cash claim
A cash release is not a permanent earnings stream
H1 FY27 CFO of INR1,101.37 crore comprises operating profit before working capital of INR598.08 crore, a
working-capital release of INR617.21 crore and INR113.92 crore tax payments. Trade-payable inflow of INR524.62 crore
is 47.6% of CFO. Receivable/inventory releases also helped. Supplier balances and inventory rebuilding can reverse these
Net cash depends on the definition
At 30 September, borrowings were INR1,904.64 crore. Cash equivalents plus current investments were INR1,895.67 crore,
leaving INR8.97 crore net borrowing before leases. Adding INR10.52 crore other bank balances gives INR1.55 crore net
cash. We exclude those bank balances from the conservative EV bridge until unrestricted status is verified. Leases of
INR500.35 crore bring lease-inclusive net debt to INR509.32 crore. [S1 p10]
Cash left after capital and financing costs
H1 CFO less cash capex of INR151.33 crore, lease principal of INR12.27 crore and total interest paid of INR68.09 crore
leaves INR869.68 crore. This levered cash bridge precedes dividends/buyback and investing items; it is not FCFF. The
same measure was INR544.36 crore in FY26 and minus INR271.79 crore in FY25. Government-grant receipts are
separately classified in investing cash flows. [S1; S2]
FY26 cash-flow adjustments removed INR198.42 crore of grant income while cash grant receipts were INR400.66 crore in
investing. A valuation that capitalises earnings and adds those receipts without reconciliation risks double counting. The
captive-power subsidiary became an associate from 31 July 2026; this changes consolidation and minorities. Forecast NCI
is reduced but not assumed zero. [S1 note8; S2 p360]

Risks, catalysts and evidence that would change the view
Large-customer ordering, tariffs/refund timing, currency and freight can alter export economics. The October filing says
tariff refunds are being received and reconciled, with remaining amounts subject to administrative processes. No unverified
tariff rate, treaty benefit or extra refund windfall is built into this valuation. [S1 note5]
Flooding disrupted Vapi from 23 July. The company disclosed an INR125 crore on-account insurance receipt and INR7.16
crore net exceptional charge. Final settlement, including loss of profit, remains subject to assessment. The FY27 estimate
carries the disclosed exceptional charge but assumes no additional claim gain. [S1 note6]
Cotton, energy and wage costs can erode margins if customer pricing lags. FY26 top-ten customer concentration rose to
65.1%, from 56.5%. Faster private-label recovery could help utilisation; loss or repricing of major accounts could quickly
A 15% operating EBITDA margin at INR13,500 crore FY28 revenue, 25% tax and 25x earnings produces about INR305.
That scenario invalidates the base valuation. Conversely, INR11,500 crore sales and a 10.5% margin produce about INR97
at 18x. Scenarios are not probabilities or price bounds.
